subject: EU processing: SCCs, operator fallback routing & export-control clarifications
messages:
From: Maria Hoffmann <maria.hoffmann@novahealth.eu>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-05-04T07:03:00Z
Subject: Clarify EU-only processing + SCCs — operator fallback scenario

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We are working through procurement + legal and have a couple of open questions on EU-only processing and the SCCs annex that are blocking our internal sign-off. High-level asks below — can you confirm whether Redwood's current SCCs + annex language and operational controls cover these scenarios?

1) Fallback routing: If a primary EU region becomes unavailable, what is the legally-covered fallback behavior under the SCCs? Specifically: is failover to a non-EU region (e.g., US) allowed under the SCCs by default, or does that require an explicit customer-level option?

2) Backups & exports: Where are backups stored geographically, and are backups covered by the same SCCs commitments? What evidence can Redwood provide that backups are erased in-region on customer deletion?

3) Operator access & export controls: In some cases we may be asked by our auditors for proof that operator access is restricted to EU-hosted operators or that operator actions are logged and subject to jurisdictional control. What artifacts can you share?

We need short, concrete answers we can share with our legal/compliance team and suggested contract language (a short clause or paragraph) we can include in our vendor addendum.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — procurement hopes to close next week if feasible.

Best,
Maria Hoffmann
Head of IT Risk & Compliance
NovaHealth GmbH

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: 2028-05-04T08:25:00Z
Subject: Re: Clarify EU-only processing + SCCs — operator fallback scenario

Hi Maria — thanks for the clear list. Short answers below; I included attachments with example wording and our operator access matrix. Happy to jump on a quick call with your legal team.

1) Fallback routing: By default Redwood routes within the EU when a customer has chosen EU-only processing. We only allow failover to non-EU regions if the customer has explicitly enabled cross-border failover in their account settings or has signed an exception in their addendum. In other words: non-EU failover is opt-in and surfaced as an explicit clause in the contract (we do not silently route EU traffic to the US).

2) Backups & exports: Backups for EU-only customers are stored in-region (EU) by default and are covered by the SCCs annex. If a customer requests cross-region export of backups, that action is logged and requires an explicit approval / export request via our procurement workflow. On deletion, backups are subject to our documented purge workflow; we can provide an attestation of deletion and a backup purge log extract (time-limited audit artifact).

3) Operator access & export controls: Operator activity is limited by role-based access controls and Just-In-Time access processes tied to MFA and KMS key scoping. We maintain operator access logs and session recordings for privileged actions; those artifacts can be produced as part of an agreed evidence bundle (redacted). For EU-only customers we can provide a scoped operator access affidavit and an export-control checklist that maps to the SCCs obligations.

Attachments: SCCs_Operator_Annex.pdf (proposed annex text), operator_access_matrix.csv (role mapping + regional entitlements).

Suggested next steps:
- I’ve attached a short addendum snippet you can share (SCCs_Operator_Annex.pdf).
- If you need formal attestation, we can prepare: operator access affidavit + backup purge extract + audit log snapshot (we typically deliver via secure link).
- I can loop in our legal lead (Lauren) for final contract language.

If helpful, I can be on a call with your legal/procurement tomorrow.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference

Looping you both in — Maria from NovaHealth has a few procurement/legal questions (below) that map to SCCs, operator access, backups and fallback routing. Please see my draft responses (sent to Maria) and two quick asks: 

- Legal ask (Lauren): Can you review the attached SCCs_Operator_Annex.pdf and propose concise contract language that we can send as a vendor addendum? Prefer short, definitive clauses (2–4 bullets/paras) that procurement can paste into their draft.

- Evidence ask (Naomi): Nova will likely request a backup purge extract and an operator access affidavit. Can you confirm what we can deliver within a 7-business-day window and provide a redaction template for the audit logs?

Key points I included in my response:
- Non-EU failover is opt-in only and requires explicit contractual exception.
- Backups are in-region by default and are covered by SCCs; exports require approval and are logged.
- Operator access is RBAC/JIT, logged and can be attested to.

Attachments included for your review: SCCs_Operator_Annex.pdf, operator_access_matrix.csv.

Thanks — procurement is asking for a turnaround by next week. Let me know if you need a short prep call.

Karthik

Karthik — saw this, thanks for the draft. High-level guidance and proposed contract snippets below. I kept the language tight so procurement can paste directly.

Proposed addendum text (short):
1) EU-Only Processing: "Vendor shall process Customer Data exclusively within the European Union unless Customer provides prior written consent authorizing cross-border failover or export. Any cross-border failover will be governed by an explicit, signed exception to this Addendum and logged in Vendor's export audit trail."

2) Backups & Deletion: "Backups for EU-Only customers will be stored and purged in-region. Upon Customer deletion request, Vendor will initiate backup purge procedures and provide an attestation and deletion log extract within 10 business days. Exception handling for legal holds will be documented and mutually agreed."

3) Operator Access & Evidence: "Vendor maintains role-based operator access, Just-In-Time privilege elevation, and cryptographic key scoping. Vendor will provide a scoped operator access affidavit and redacted audit log snapshot upon reasonable request under a mutual NDA. Production of full session recordings requires customer consent or legal process."

Evidence timeline (Naomi): please confirm availability, but standard deliverables we can promise within 7 business days:
- Redacted operator access affidavit (template ready)
- Backup purge log extract (redacted by snapshot id)
- Export audit trail for any cross-border events (if any)

Rishi — flag any export-control or sanctions checks we should run before handing over log extracts to Nova.

I’ll attach a plain-text version of the addendum wording. Karthik — if Maria confirms they want the addendum we should route to legal for signature and coordinate delivery of the evidence bundle.

-Lauren
